title: Divergence commutes with convolution by a locally integrable kernel
statement: Let n ∈ ℕ and E = ℝⁿ with Lebesgue measure. Let κ : E → ℝ be locally integrable and g : E → E a C¹ vector field with compact support. Then for every x ∈ E, div(κ * g)(x) = (κ * div g)(x). Here κ * g = convolution κ g (lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume, i.e. (κ * g)(x) = ∫ κ(t) g(x − t) dt; κ * div g is the scalar convolution; and div = Chapter02.euclideanDivergence, the trace of the Fréchet derivative.
lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (κ : Rn n → ℝ) (g : Rn n → Rn n), LocallyIntegrable κ volume → ContDiff ℝ 1 g → HasCompactSupport g → ∀ x, Chapter02.euclideanDivergence (convolution κ g (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume) x = convolution κ (Chapter02.euclideanDivergence g) (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume x
